script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: THE REMEDY

INT. DR. ALEX'S OFFICE - DAY

DR. ALEX LYNCH, a mid-forties psychiatrist with a warm smile and a gentle voice, sits behind a desk adorned with plants and books. A large window behind him lets in the sunlight. A soft knock echoes through the room.

DR. LYNCH
(looking up)
Come in.

The door opens. In walks EVELYN REYNOLDS, a woman in her late thirties, dressed in a business suit and carrying a briefcase. Her eyes are filled with fear and determination.

---

INT. DR. LYNCH'S OFFICE - A FEW MINUTES LATER

---

EVELYN
(nervously)
I've never done this before.

DR. LYNCH
(sympathetically)
It's okay, Evelyn. You're here because you want to change something in your life. That takes courage.

EVELYN
(sighs)
I lost everything, Dr. Lynch. My career, my husband, even my friends. I can't go back to that life.

---

INT. EVELYN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Evelyn sits alone on her sofa, surrounded by empty alcohol bottles. She looks distressed and disheveled. A phone rings. She hesitates before answering.

---

EVELYN
(voice shaking)
Hello?

DR. LYNCH
(voice over phone)
Evelyn, it's Dr. Lynch. How are you tonight?

EVELYN
(tearfully)
I've been better.

---

INT. DR. LYNCH'S OFFICE - DAY

---

DR. LYNCH
(firmly)
Evelyn, I want you to know that no matter what you've done or how far you've fallen, there's always a chance for redemption.

---

INT. EVELYN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Evelyn, looking better but still struggling, goes to a local shelter and volunteers to help out. She meets JASMINE, a young woman with a bright smile and an infectious energy.

---

JASMINE
(smiling)
You look like you've seen better days, but I can see the good in you, Evelyn.

---

INT. DR. LYNCH'S OFFICE - DAY

---

DR. LYNCH
(encouragingly)
That's the spirit, Evelyn. You're on the right path.

---

INT. LOCAL COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

Evelyn and Jasmine work together at the community center, helping those in need. Evelyn finds purpose in her life and starts to rebuild her relationships with her family and friends.

---

INT. DR. LYNCH'S OFFICE - DAY

---

DR. LYNCH
(smiling)
Evelyn, you've made great progress. I'm proud of you.

EVELYN
(tearfully)
Thank you, Dr. Lynch. I couldn't have done it without you.

---

EXT. PARK - DAY

Evelyn and her husband, REUBEN, sit on a park bench, holding hands. They talk about their past mistakes and their future plans.

---

REUBEN
(serious)
I know I hurt you, Evelyn, but I want to make things right. I want us to start over.

EVELYN
(smiling)
I want that too, Reuben.

---

INT. DR. LYNCH'S OFFICE - DAY

---

DR. LYNCH
(smiling)
Evelyn, you've been given a second chance. Don't waste it.

---

FADE OUT.

THE END
